headline: Peace-deal rumour flips oil from $110 to a loss; weak US housing trims yields, Bunds rally
summary: Oil hit five-month highs early, with Brent near $112 and expiring November WTI at $110.48, then reversed on an unconfirmed report of a US–Iran deal: WTI settled down 1.8% at $101.79 and RBOB fell 2.3% to a seven-week low. A slump in housing data nudged the 10-year down about 2bp to near 5.12% while gold slipped and silver gained about 1.5%. In Europe, Bunds rallied on the oil turn as French debt lagged, keeping the OAT–Bund spread near 150bp.
drivers: Oil: risk premium meets a deal headline

Brent topped $111 and November WTI hit $110.48 on more Hormuz tanker attacks (18 in two weeks, per Kpler), then an unconfirmed US–Iran deal report knocked crude down as much as 3.3%. Bloomberg later called the report inaccurate, but Brent still settled 0.7% lower at $108.79 and December WTI at $97.82.

September housing starts fell to 1.22M against 1.30M expected and pending home sales dropped 7.3% versus a 0.4% forecast, pulling the 10-year about 2bp lower to near 5.12%, while the 2-year rose about 2bp and the 2s10s curve flattened about 5bp.

Lower oil helped euro-area bonds: the 10-year Bund fell about 4–7bp to near 3.39–3.42% and the Schatz about 5bp. French yields touched 4.99% before easing, so the OAT–Bund spread stayed near 150–153bp as new protests were called for Saturday and the budget debate slipped to Oct 27.
Fed: no October hike, December still priced
Futures give only about a 15% chance of a hike on Oct 28 but around 90% for one by December, keeping real yields high and gold below $4,150 even as the dollar index eased about 0.25% to near 101.7.

oil.note: Expiring Nov WTI fell $1.87 (-1.8%) to $101.79 after a $110.48 high; Dec WTI $97.82, Brent $108.79.
oil.why: Crude spiked early as Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping intensified, with 30 incidents logged this month and Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi sites, lifting Brent near $112. An unconfirmed report that Washington and Tehran were close to a deal triggered a sharp unwind from CTA positioning at 100% long. Bloomberg later said the report was inaccurate, which trimmed the losses, but expiry-day selling left November WTI $8.70 below its high.
oil.outlook: Bias firm but volatile in a $97–112 Brent range: Hormuz flows near half of normal keep a floor, while crowded longs and pre-midterm deal hopes make rallies fragile. A confirmed reopening would break $97; a weekly close above $112 opens the spring highs.
oil.watch: EIA stocks Wed Oct 21 (API showed a 4.9M-barrel draw), US–Iran talk headlines, OPEC+ Nov 1 and the Nov 3 midterms.

gas.note: RBOB Nov settled down 7.4¢ (-2.3%) at $3.1172, lowest since Sept 2; pump average $4.28, down 4.7¢.
gas.why: Gasoline fell harder than crude as the reversal in oil met a market already pricing more Russian diesel and products under the sanctions waiver and the end of summer demand. Gasoline stocks built for two straight weeks, the winter-blend switch is cutting costs, and the crack to Brent narrowed sharply. The EIA's weekly survey put the pump average at $4.284 a gallon, down 4.7¢, while diesel rose 9.7¢ to $6.28.
gas.outlook: Soft bias in a $3.00–3.30 range as the crack compresses into winter; crude near $100 limits the downside. A clear gasoline draw in Wednesday's data would steady it near $3.20, while a crude break below $97 would put $3.00 in play.
gas.watch: EIA gasoline stocks Wed Oct 21 (seen flat; API showed a 2M draw), the November contract's expiry at month-end and the pump average.

gold.note: Spot near $4,125 (-0.3%); December futures settled down 0.4% at $4,142.60.
gold.why: Gold slipped even though Treasury yields and oil fell, because the market's focus stays on a likely December Fed hike, priced at about 90%. Lower oil cut the inflation scare that had supported haven demand, and Treasuries, not gold, are drawing defensive money at 5%-plus yields. A softer dollar, down about 0.25%, limited the decline.
gold.outlook: Range $4,075–4,200 into the Oct 28 Fed, with a mild downside tilt while the 10-year holds above 5%. A dovish hold that lowers December odds would lift it through $4,200; a break below $4,073 would target $4,000.
gold.watch: The Fed on Oct 27–28, US yields, the dollar and PCE inflation.

silver.note: Spot up about 1.5% to near $57.80; gold/silver ratio back near 71.
silver.why: Silver outperformed gold as falling oil and yields lifted cyclical assets: the Russell 2000 rose 1.8% and the Dow 1%. Its industrial demand profile benefits from a softer dollar and easing energy costs, and it rebounded from Monday's $56.70 low in Asia. Weak US housing data is the main brake on further gains.
silver.outlook: Recovering but still capped below $60. Holding $56.30 keeps a move toward $58.70–59.40 in play; a close below $55.40 would reopen the July lows.
silver.watch: Risk appetite, the dollar, Chinese demand and the Fed on Oct 28.

us2y.note: Near 4.79%, up about 2bp; October hike odds about 15%, December near 90%.
us2y.why: The 2-year edged higher while longer yields fell, as traders kept pricing a December hike even after soft housing data. The Fed is in its blackout, so short-end pricing is anchored to last week's message of no urgency for October but further tightening by year-end, with CPI running at 3.7%.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.70–4.85% until the meeting. A hawkish statement or hot PCE would test 4.85%; a dovish hold that cuts December odds would take it back toward 4.70%.
us2y.watch: The Fed's Oct 27–28 decision, then PCE.

us5y.note: About 4.92%, down roughly 1bp, little changed as the curve flattened.
us5y.why: The 5-year barely moved: lower oil and the 7.3% drop in pending home sales pulled yields down, but firm December hike pricing kept the belly anchored near the 2-year. Inflation near 3.7% keeps buyers cautious around 4.90%.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.85–5.05%. Oil and Fed guidance on December decide it; a clear hike signal would lift the belly toward 5%.
us5y.watch: Oil, the Oct 21 20-year auction and the Oct 28 Fed.

us10y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.12% (Dow Jones: 5.116%), ending a two-day rise.
us10y.why: September housing starts fell 5.2% to 1.22M against 1.30M expected, and pending home sales fell 7.3% against a 0.4% forecast, showing 5%-plus mortgage rates hurting demand. Oil's reversal from five-month highs added support. The rally stayed small because firm December Fed pricing kept the short end steady, so the 2s10s curve flattened about 5bp to near 33bp.
us10y.outlook: Range 5.00–5.30%. Weak housing, fading October hike odds and hopes of lighter long-bond supply cap it, while oil near $100 keeps it above 5%. A close above 5.31% would restart the selloff; below 5.00% needs oil to break.
us10y.watch: The $13B 20-year reopening Wed Oct 21, oil, the Fed on Oct 28 and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: About 5.43%, down roughly 3bp; the long end led the rally.
us30y.why: The 30-year fell the most on the curve as weak housing data and lower oil eased long-run inflation worries. Talk that Treasury may trim long-bond auction sizes at the Nov 4 refunding is also supporting the long end, ahead of Wednesday's 20-year sale.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.55%. A solid 20-year auction and confirmation of smaller long-bond sizes would flatten the curve further; no change at the refunding would add term premium back.
us30y.watch: The 20-year auction Wed Oct 21 and the Nov 4 refunding.

de2y.note: About 3.05–3.08%, down roughly 2–5bp as oil eased.
de2y.why: The Schatz fell as crude's reversal took some pressure off energy-driven inflation, which pushed euro-area CPI to 3.8% in September. Markets still lean towards another ECB hike, but in December rather than at the Oct 29 meeting, with the deposit rate at 2.50%.
de2y.outlook: Range 3.00–3.15%. The ECB's Oct 29 guidance decides it; a firm December signal would lift it toward 3.15%.
de2y.watch: ECB decision Oct 29 and flash October inflation.

de5y.note: Near 3.16–3.19%, a few bp lower with the wider Bund rally.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund followed oil lower in the afternoon and drew some haven demand from French unrest. Gains were limited because persistent energy costs keep the market from pricing out further ECB tightening.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.10–3.30% into the ECB. More French stress keeps it pinned; a hawkish ECB or an oil rebound would push it higher.
de5y.watch: ECB Oct 29, oil and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: Down about 4–7bp to near 3.39–3.42%, the low end of this month's range.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund rallied as oil turned lower and US yields fell, with Reuters putting it 7bp down at 3.385% late in the day. Haven flows from France's unrest added to demand. The Treasury–Bund gap stayed wide near 170bp, which reflects higher US policy rates.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.35–3.55%. Germany benefits from French stress and softer oil; a move back above 3.50% would need a hawkish ECB or a renewed oil spike.
de10y.watch: ECB Oct 29, oil and German supply.

de30y.note: About 3.75%, slightly lower; the long end tracked global yields.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund edged down with US long bonds after the weak housing data and oil's reversal. The move was smaller than at the 10-year because global long-end supply concerns and term premium still weigh on the long end.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.70–3.90%. It follows US long bonds more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US 20-year auction, US long-end yields and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.63–3.66%, little changed; short OATs remain tied to the ECB.
fr2y.why: The 2-year OAT was steady as short-dated French paper tracks ECB pricing rather than fiscal risk. It did not join the Schatz rally, a sign that the political premium is starting to reach shorter maturities.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.55–3.70%; it would jump only if a censure motion brought down the government.
fr2y.watch: Protests on Saturday Oct 24, the budget debate resuming Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr5y.note: About 4.27%, roughly flat as France lagged the Bund rally.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT held near Monday's levels while German yields fell, as protest groups called a fresh round of demonstrations for Saturday after the weekend riots. The National Assembly put off the budget's revenue vote, extending doubts about the 2027 plan to bring the deficit to 5% of GDP.
fr5y.outlook: Bias higher while the budget is unresolved; range 4.20–4.40%. A calm weekend and a clean revenue vote would ease pressure.
fr5y.watch: Saturday's protests and the budget debate from Oct 27.

fr10y.note: Hit 4.99% intraday, then eased to near 4.88–4.94%; OAT–Bund spread about 150–153bp.
fr10y.why: French 10-year yields rose to 4.988% early, close to the 4.99% peak of early October that was the highest since 2002, as investors priced more protests and a fraught budget. They eased as oil fell, but much less than Bunds, so the spread widened about 3–5bp to around 150bp. The revenue vote expected Tuesday was deferred, and debate is set to resume Oct 27.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias wider in a 140–160bp range, since investors doubt real fiscal consolidation before the 2027 presidential race. A daily close above 5% would mark a new 24-year high; the ECB is unlikely to step in unless trading becomes disorderly.
fr10y.watch: Protests Sat Oct 24, the budget debate Oct 27, the ECB Oct 29 and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: About 5.45–5.47%, near flat; the long end holds most of Monday's jump.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT kept most of Monday's 6bp rise, with the long end carrying the largest fiscal premium as debt service is projected to top €91 billion in 2027. Lower oil and the global long-end rally prevented further losses.
fr30y.outlook: The most exposed part of the curve if the budget stalls or ratings are cut. A break above 5.55% would retest this month's highs.
fr30y.watch: The budget debate and long-dated OAT auctions.

watch: Next: EIA stocks and the US 20-year auction on Wednesday, French protests on Saturday, the French budget debate and Fed meeting from Oct 27, the ECB on Oct 29, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms on Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
